# Combat Standard Operating Procedure
This procedure binds [bold]every player[/bold] the moment a fight becomes possible - crew, Security, command, silicons and antagonists alike. It does not matter who started it, who is winning it, or whether the other side deserves it. The aim is a round worth playing for everyone in it, not the fastest possible kill.
If you are wondering whether this applies to you, it does.
## Engage in Numbers
Do not rush someone alone. A lone attacker forces a kill-or-be-killed exchange and ends the encounter before a word is spoken.
Call it in, wait for backup, and move as a group. Numbers even the odds, and even odds are what make an arrest, a surrender or a conversation possible instead of a body.
This cuts both ways. A passenger swinging first because they found a weapon is the same failure as an officer doing it, and gets the same response.
## No Valid Hunting
Do not go hunting the moment you suspect somebody. Confirm it, report it, and plan the approach.
Suspicion is not a licence, and neither is a rumour on the radio, an unfamiliar face in maintenance, or somebody being somewhere you would rather they were not. Lethal force on sight is a last resort, and more often than not it should not be your opening move. Someone left alive gives the shift somewhere to go; a corpse in a hallway does not.
## Nobody Is Exempt
Rank, role and grievance do not buy an exception.
- [bold]Crew[/bold] do not get to swarm a suspect because somebody shouted over the radio. You are not deputised, and a mob is not an investigation. - [bold]Security[/bold] are held to this hardest, because they carry the tools that make ignoring it easy. The force ladder is in [textlink="Security SOP" link="GuideSecuritySOP"]. - [bold]Command[/bold] [bold]shall not[/bold] lead a charge, and [bold]shall not[/bold] order one. Directing the crew to swarm a suspect is the same failure as doing it yourself, with more bodies. - [bold]Antagonists[/bold] are bound by the mirror of this procedure. Play the round out rather than rushing people down the moment you are able. See [textlink="Antagonist SOP" link="GuideAntagonistSOP"].
## When Speed Is Justified
This procedure is not a demand that you stand still and die.
You may act immediately, alone, and with whatever force the situation needs, where waiting would plainly cost a life or lose the station - an active shooter mid-massacre, a bomb about to go off, someone already dragging a victim away. The test is whether a slower option genuinely existed, not whether a faster one was available.
Being attacked first does not end your obligations here. It ends your obligation to wait.
## If Someone Ignores This
[bold]Ahelp it.[/bold] Do not settle it in-round by treating the next person the way you were treated - that turns one player's bad shift into everybody's.
[italic]For the rules governing conduct in a fight, see [textlink="Section 11. Antagonists" link="RuleC11"].[/italic]
